answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to earn trust through verifiable work, like a juniper that only roots after seasons of care. New agents start on a low mesa of trust with capped transaction limits and must complete audited tasks whose outputs peers verify before limits rise. Creating a thousand fakes then costs a thousand times the verified work, not just key generation. A sable audit trail of signed task receipts lets the network spot clusters copying identical behaviour and quarantine them before they vote or claim rewards, so fakes stay expensive and unprofitable.
